title.narrative: Second Urban Environmental Management in the Tonle Sap Basin Project

description.narrative: The proposed project will support the government of Cambodia in improving urban services and enhancing climate resilience in participating towns in the Tonle Sap Basin. The project will support improve urban services in wastewater management, solid waste management and drainage in the provincial cities of Battambang (Battambang Province), Serei Saophoan (Banteay Meanchey Province) and Stueng Saen (Kampong Thom Province). The project will also improve institutional effectiveness and improve the policy and planning environment.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Institutional effectiveness improved Indicator: 25 government staff (including 10 women) reported increased knowledge on urban service delivery, urban facilities O&M, and private partnerships and other institutional arrangements Achievement: 41 (4 women) Progress/Status: 73 government staff (including 25 women) reported increased knowledge of urban service delivery, urban facilities O&M, and private partnerships and other institutional arrangements. Data Source: Training records Actual value: 41 (4 women)

Output: Institutional effectiveness improved Indicator: Semi-autonomous urban service units established and operational Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: (i) USUs for all cities have been established; but not yet been allocated enough staff required and/or officially approved by government; and (ii) SWMUs for all cities have been established and all positions have been filled.
Data Source: Project progress reports

Output: Urban environmental infrastructure improved Indicator: New drainage networks constructed Achievement: 27 Progress/Status: Construction of drainage systems in: - Stueng Saen: 23.35 km completed. - Serei Saophoan: 5.03 km out of 5.86 km planned completed. Total: 29.211 km
Data Source: Construction records, project progress reports

Output: Urban environmental infrastructure improved Indicator: New sewer networks constructed Achievement: 195 Progress/Status: Construction of sewer networks in: - Stueng Saen: 44 km completed. - Battambang: 97.32 km completed. - Serei Saophoan: 108.01 km out of 121.19 km completed. Total: 262.51 km Data Source: Construction records, project progress reports

Output: Urban environmental infrastructure improved Indicator: New wastewater treatment plants with 9,600 m3/day capacity constructed Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Construction of wastewater treatment plants in: - Stueng Saen (3,500 m3/day) completed - Battambang (8,500 m3/day) and Serei Saophoan (3,500 m3/day) are ongoing. Total: 15,500 m3/day
Data Source: Construction records, project progress reports

Output: Urban environmental infrastructure improved Indicator: Staff employed in O&M are women Achievement: 13-19 Progress/Status: There are two levels of Committee in each O&M structure for wastewater (USU) and landfill (SWMU):
Stung Sen: 6/22= 27% USU 1/7= 14% SWMU
Serei Saophoan: 8/21 =38% USU 2/24= 8% SWMU
Battambang: 8/33= 25% USU 6/20= 30% SWMU
Accumulating, project could reach 23.5% of women represented in O&M committee. Data Source: Construction records, project progress reports Actual value: 13-19

Output: Urban environmental infrastructure improved Indicator: Controlled landfills with 528,000 m3 capacity constructed and operational Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Construction of Landfills in: - Battambang (313,973m3) and Stueng Saen (97,886m3)) completed. - Serei Saophoan (171,874m3) is completed. Total volume (583,733m3)
Data Source: Construction records, project progress reports

Output: Policy and planning environment improved Indicator: Provincial spatial plan for Banteay Meancheay and land use master plans for Stueng Saen and Serei Saophoan, with climate resilience and gender responsive measures, developed and approved Achievement: Y Progress/Status: 100% of completion. During the September 2024 review mission and the 2024 Midterm Review (MTR), the Project Management Unit (PMU) informed that, following a government decision, the official titles of the planning documents were revised. Specifically, the “Urban Development Strategy and Master Plan” was renamed to “Land Use Master Plan (LUMP)” for Stueng Sean and Serei Saophoan, and to “Provincial Spatial Plan (PSP)” for Banteay Meanchey. The term LUMP was not used for Battambang as a LUMP already exists for that area.
The planning documents have been completed and submitted to the Ministry of Land Management, Urban Planning and Construction (MLMUPC), which has agreed with the content and initiated the formal government approval process. The PMU will continue to support MLMUPC in securing official approval, which is anticipated by 2026. Additionally, gender-responsive measures have been developed and approved as standalone documents. Data Source: Project progress reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Policy and planning environment improved Indicator: Road map for financial sustainability (including tariff road map) developed between MPWT and three provincial governments, with consultation from MEF, MIH, MOWA, MRD and other relevant agencies Achievement: Y Progress/Status: The financial sustainability road map has been finalized, and the next activity is to support MPWT/PMU in the interministerial meetings, which will be tentatively conducted before the end of 2025, to have the proposed tariff structure approved to be included in the joint bills with clean water. It is important to note that MEF approved on 20 March 2025 the O&M budgets for Battambang and Stung Saen wastewater treatment plants operations as the temporary arrangement before the joint billing system implementation or other additional support. Data Source: Project progress reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
Urban services improved in participating cities

People (8,040 women) benefit from reduced flooding through improved drainage Achievement: 28318 Progress/Status: Constructions of Drainage for Stueng Saen, Battambang, are completed and in operation. Serei Saophoan drainage network is ongoing. In two cities, the drainage systems are currently serving 28,318 people, including 14,513 women. This represents 180% of the original target of 8,040. Once the Serei Sorphoan drainage system is fully operational, the number of beneficiaries is expected to increase by up to twofold. Data Source: Annual reports by DPWTs and MPWT; monitoring reports, ADB loan missions, project completion report

People (96,700 women) served by improved solid waste management Achievement: 179627 Progress/Status: Based actual check with SWMU as well as respective municipalities in September 2025, 40,263 HHs are currently served by improved SWM, of which 26,043 HHs at Battambang, 11,190 HHs at Serei Saophoan and 3,030 HHs at Stung Sen. Hence, 179.,627 beneficiaries, of which 88,162 beneficiaries are females. Data Source: Annual reports by DPWTs and MPWT; monitoring reports, ADB loan missions, project completion report

People (23,739 women) serviced by new and improved wastewater collection and treatment facilities Achievement: 50088 Progress/Status: Based on the progress update from the contractors, the total number of connections across the three cities reached 11,554, serving 50,088 people in total, of whom 25,404 are women. Compared to the original target, this represents 107.01% achievement. Since one of the three cities is still in the process of building connections, the beneficiary name list is still being finalized. It is expected that the number of people served will increase by the next quarter, along with the completion of the project report. Data Source: Annual reports by DPWTs and MPWT; monitoring reports, ADB loan missions, project completion report
